338dd5d153.q: What mental health challenges do Black entrepreneurs face while building their business?
338dd5d153.a: Black entrepreneurs face compounded pressure from being Black in America and simultaneously running a business. This adds a different arsenal of pressure, making it easy to get wrapped up in proving haters wrong and goal orientation to the point of neglecting eating, sleeping, and taking breaks, especially when working a nine-to-five job while running a side business.
338dd5d153.e: Episode 1.5 - Mental Health As A Black Entrepreneur

d07a8a8a36.q: How can business owners prevent mental health breakdowns from overwork and stress?
d07a8a8a36.a: Business owners should take time away from the grind to keep themselves aligned and in check. This can be as simple as taking a day off and laying in bed, spending time with family or friends, or going to places that bring you back to reality and keep you grounded. Setting firm boundaries is essential, including not responding to anyone on designated days off and communicating this to customers in advance.
d07a8a8a36.e: Episode 1.5 - Mental Health As A Black Entrepreneur

42c67c335f.q: Why should entrepreneurs celebrate small wins instead of only focusing on major goals?
42c67c335f.a: Small wins should be celebrated because they represent real progress and momentum. Enjoying small wins on the journey keeps morale high and creates memory markers that make achieving larger goals feel more rewarding. Additionally, when working in service-based industries dealing with different people daily, acknowledging progress like gaining one new customer or follower maintains motivation and prevents getting lost in pursuing only the end goal.
42c67c335f.e: Episode 1.5 - Mental Health As A Black Entrepreneur

7f05b1aaa6.q: What scheduling strategy can entrepreneurs use when working both a nine-to-five job and a side business?
7f05b1aaa6.a: Entrepreneurs should map out their schedule to give themselves a few hours to work on their business while also allocating hours to recover and reset. Another approach is working intensively for three days straight and taking the fourth day completely off to recharge. The key is planning deliberately rather than working 24/7, as the nine-to-five is the main income source until the business takes off.
7f05b1aaa6.e: Episode 1.5 - Mental Health As A Black Entrepreneur

2cd9867c27.q: How should Black entrepreneurs handle imposter syndrome and self-doubt while building their empire?
2cd9867c27.a: Build your empire brick by brick and appreciate the incremental progress. If you lay down two bricks today, that is two more bricks than you had yesterday. Give yourself credit and recognize that building a business is difficult work that many people are not doing. Reflecting on growth from having five customers to fifty to five hundred helps combat self-doubt by documenting real progress.
2cd9867c27.e: Episode 1.5 - Mental Health As A Black Entrepreneur

4703888720.q: Should you invest in product materials or marketing knowledge first when launching a product?
4703888720.a: You should definitely invest in your materials first before advertising. You need to know what your product looks like and feels like by ordering samples before doing anything else, because you need to have confidence in your product to sell it effectively. Once you confirm your sample and are ready to sell, then you invest in knowledge on marketing to understand your core audience and target customers.
4703888720.e: Episode 2 - Should I Invest In Knowledge Or Products First?

caa355db1f.q: What is Jiffy Shirts and why is it recommended for ordering blank apparel?
caa355db1f.a: Jiffy Shirts (JiffyShirts.com) is a website that sells blank apparel of all brands without order minimums, so you can order one or two shirts. They carry hoodies, sweats, joggers, and brands like Gildan, Bella Canvas, Hanes, and Fruit of the Loom. It is recommended as a good starting point for beginners who don't have much to work with or don't want to do too much too fast.
caa355db1f.e: Episode 2 - Should I Invest In Knowledge Or Products First?

6ec43b20ab.q: What is a resale certificate and why do you need one for wholesale blank purchases?
6ec43b20ab.a: A resale certificate is a document you file within your county, city, and state that permits you to buy wholesale and resell what you're buying within your estate. Many places won't even sell to you without a resale certificate. In Florida, you can apply for one online and if approved they send it to you in the mail. Once you have it, you can apply for wholesale accounts with companies like Bella Canvas.
6ec43b20ab.e: Episode 2 - Should I Invest In Knowledge Or Products First?

069029ef29.q: Why does Bella Canvas material quality differ from standard Gildan t-shirts?
069029ef29.a: Bella Canvas uses 100 percent heirloom cotton that is combed and ring spun, making it really soft, whereas Gildan tees are 100 percent cotton that is not combed or ring spun. You can tell a total quality difference between them. Additionally, Gildan tees shrink because they're 100 percent cotton, so customers should hang dry items instead of using the dryer to avoid losing inches.
069029ef29.e: Episode 2 - Should I Invest In Knowledge Or Products First?

5094f48a30.q: How much does a sample cost from a manufacturer for custom cut and sew products?
5094f48a30.a: Samples from a manufacturer that cuts and sews an item from raw materials typically run anywhere between 150 to 300 dollars for one item. Most manufacturers will deduct the sample price from your bulk order after you verify the price, so it is not a complete waste of money but rather an investment in testing the product before selling to the public.
5094f48a30.e: Episode 2 - Should I Invest In Knowledge Or Products First?

20383bf828.q: What monthly income and expense structure should you establish before investing in a business?
20383bf828.a: At an $11 per hour job working 40 hours per week, you take home approximately 650 dollars every two weeks or about 1,300 dollars per month after taxes. If your monthly expenses for rent, utilities, food, and transportation total $1,000, you would have $300 left. You should not invest all $300 into your business; instead, save $150-$250 per paycheck until you reach a startup amount of $1,000 to $3,000-$500 before starting, depending on your comfort level.
20383bf828.e: Episode 2 - Should I Invest In Knowledge Or Products First?

ce9a8c0436.q: What is the difference between a logo and actual branding?
ce9a8c0436.a: A logo is not branding at all—it's just a logo. Branding is the environment and culture that you promote, what your brand stands for, and the meaning behind your brand. A logo, graphics, flyers, and business cards would actually fall more into promotion because they are what you use to promote your brand. Branding is what people think about your brand or your company—it's the reputation your business has and what people know you for.

2da8c88b6a.q: What does branding actually mean according to design experts?
2da8c88b6a.a: A brand is the result of what customers think about your product, service, or company. It ends up in their heads and hearts—they take whatever raw materials you throw at them and create something out of it. Every customer has a different brand of you, so when you create a brand, you're creating millions of brands. A brand is a reputation, and it's affected by everything: your products, messaging, design, culture, and how employees behave.

93af1049dc.q: How does personal opinion on social media affect brand reputation?
93af1049dc.a: Once you become a brand or own a brand, certain things you have to stay away from because you don't want to tarnish your brand. Business owners don't chime in on taboo topics because people might confuse the intent of your brand with your personal opinion. Everything you do affects your brand—whether it's your personal time, what you do in a club, or what you say in church. It's always going to reflect on your brand, always.

2cc39f319d.q: What percentage of business revenue should be reinvested back into the company?
2cc39f319d.a: If you make a thousand dollars in a week, at least 60 percent of it needs to go back into the business, mandatory. You made a thousand and you're putting that money back into your business to make another thousand or two thousand, or to double or triple your money. You can't make a thousand, put in a hundred and expect to make another thousand—it doesn't work that way because you have to market and promote your business, and effective marketing and promotion costs.
